steps.title: Prepare 1x TE buffer
steps.instruction: Calculate the total 1x TE volume needed (200 µl per sample, 100 µl per standard, plus 300‑400 µl for DNA‑standard dilution). Example for a high‑range run with 20 samples and 8 standards: 20 × 200 µl + 8 × 100 µl + 300 µl = 5 100 µl; prepare ~5 500 µl to allow for pipetting loss. Dilute the supplied 20× TE stock: volume of 20× TE = final volume ÷ 20; add water to reach the final volume (e.g., for 5 ml total, mix 250 µl 20× TE with 4 750 µl water).

steps.title: Dilute DNA standard
steps.instruction: Prepare working DNA‑standard dilutions from the 100 µg ml⁻¹ stock supplied in the PicoGreen kit:

substeps.instruction: High range (2 ng µl⁻¹): mix 6 µl DNA stock with 294 µl 1× TE.
Middle range (0.5 ng µl⁻¹): mix 2 µl DNA stock with 398 µl 1× TE.
High‑sensitivity (0.05 ng µl⁻¹): first mix 2 µl DNA stock with 18 µl 1× TE (working solution); then mix 2 µl of this working solution with 398 µl 1× TE.

steps.title: Dilute PicoGreen reagent
steps.instruction: Determine the volume of 1:200 diluted PicoGreen required: (number of standards + unknown samples) × 100 µl plus extra for pipetting loss. Example: 8 standards + 20 samples = 28 × 100 µl = 2 800 µl; prepare ~3 000 µl. Dilute PicoGreen with 1× TE: PicoGreen volume = final volume ÷ 200; TE volume = final volume – PicoGreen volume (e.g., 15 µl PicoGreen + 2 985 µl 1× TE). Keep the diluted reagent protected from light until use.

steps.title: Set up 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Use NUNC 96‑well flat‑bottom black plates, cover with aluminium foil inside the lid, and label the lid with sample identifiers. Sketch the plate layout and plan the standard curve:

substeps.instruction: High‑range curve (2 µl sample): 0–100 ng µl⁻¹.
Medium‑range curve (2 µl sample): 0–25 ng µl⁻¹.
Low‑range curve (2 µl sample): 0–2.5 ng µl⁻¹.
Measure each sample in duplicate whenever possible.

steps.title: Add TE to wells
steps.instruction: Add 1× TE to each well before sample or standard addition:

substeps.instruction: Add the volume specified in Tables 1‑3 to each standard well.
Add 95‑98 µl 1× TE to each sample well (e.g., 98 µl TE for a 2 µl sample, 95 µl TE for a 5 µl sample).
Prepare two duplicate wells for each sample.

steps.title: Add DNA samples
steps.instruction: Pipette 2‑5 µl of each DNA sample into its designated wells (duplicates).

steps.title: Add DNA standards
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate diluted DNA standard (from step 2) to each standard well according to the high, medium, or low range tables.

steps.title: Add diluted PicoGreen
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of the 1:200 diluted PicoGreen reagent to every well (samples and standards) and mix by pipetting 5‑10 times.

steps.title: Incubate and read fluorescence
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature in the dark for at least 5 minutes (00:05:00), then measure fluorescence with a plate reader (seek assistance if this is your first use).

steps.title: Calculate DNA concentrations
steps.instruction: Create a calibration curve in Excel (fluorescence = x‑axis, total DNA = y‑axis using the ng values from the standard tables). Fit a trendline, obtain its equation, and calculate the DNA amount (ng) in each sample. Divide this amount by the volume of DNA added in step 6 (2‑5 µl) to obtain the concentration in ng µl⁻¹.
